newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh cent bank reserves rise by one third in '96.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh cent bank reserves rise by one third in '96.

text.p: Kazakhstan's net reserves of hard currency and gold rose by one third in 1996 to 101.9 billion tenge ($1.3 billion) at the start of this year, the National Bank of Kazakhstan said on Tuesday.
The 25.6 billion tenge rise comprised a rise of 15.3 billion tenge in gold reserves, with reserves of foreign currency growing by 10.3 billion tenge, it said in a report.
The report provided no data for the amount of gold sitting in the former Soviet republic's vaults.

But it said foreign currency reserves were boosted by 43 percent in December last year after the bank bought hard currency from the finance ministry following its successful $200 million debut Eurobond.
